chapters.title: Chapter 1 — The Worlds Where the Souls Go After Death
chapters.titleSanskrit: प्रथम अध्याय — मृत्यु के पश्चात आत्माओं का गमन

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे एव एतं देवयानं पन्थानमापद्यन्ते ये एतदेवं विदुः | अथ यो न विद्वान् पितृयाणेन पन्थना एति ||
verses.transliteration: sarve eva etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānamāpadyante ye etadevaṃ viduḥ | atha yo na vidvān pitṛyāṇena panthana eti ||
verses.translation: All those who know this go by the path of the gods (devayana). But the one who does not know this travels by the path of the ancestors (pitriyana).
verses.hindi: जो इसे जानते हैं, वे सभी देवयान मार्ग से जाते हैं। परन्तु जो नहीं जानता, वह पितृयान मार्ग से जाता है।
verses.commentary: The Kaushitaki's central distinction: devayana is the path of those who have realised Brahman — they merge with the sun, then with the cosmic fire, and do not return to rebirth. Pitriyana is the cycle of those who have acted without realisation — they enjoy the fruits of their karma and return.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kaushitaki's central distinction: devayana is the path of those who have realised Brahman — they merge with the sun, then with the cosmic fire, and do not return to rebirth. Pitriyana is the cycle of those who have acted without realisation — they enjoy the fruits of their karma and return.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणो ब्रह्मेति ह स्माह कौषीतकिः | न मनो न वाक् — प्राणमेव ब्रह्मोपास्स्व ||
verses.transliteration: prāṇo brahmeti ha smāha kauṣītakiḥ | na mano na vāk — prāṇameva brahmopāssva ||
verses.translation: Prana is Brahman — so said Kaushitaki. Not the mind, not speech — worship prana alone as Brahman.
verses.hindi: कौषीतकि ने कहा: प्राण ही ब्रह्म है। न मन, न वाणी — प्राण को ही ब्रह्म रूप से उपासना करो।
verses.commentary: The Kaushitaki Upanishad's radical reduction: in the hierarchy of consciousness, prana — the vital breath, the animating force — is supreme. Speech depends on prana; mind depends on prana; senses depend on prana.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kaushitaki Upanishad's radical reduction: in the hierarchy of consciousness, prana — the vital breath, the animating force — is supreme. Speech depends on prana; mind depends on prana; senses depend on prana.

verses.sanskrit: स एतं देवयानं पन्थानमासद्यग्निलोकमागच्छति स वायुलोकं स वरुणलोकं स आदित्यलोकं स इन्द्रलोकं स प्रजापतिलोकं स ब्रह्मलोकम् ||
verses.transliteration: sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānamāsadyagnilokamāgacchati sa vāyulokaṃ sa varuṇalokaṃ s ādityalokaṃ sa indralokaṃ sa prajāpatilokaṃ sa brahmalokam ||
verses.translation: He going by the path of the gods reaches the world of Agni, then Vayu, then Varuna, then Aditya, then Indra, then Prajapati, then the world of Brahma.
verses.hindi: वह देवयान मार्ग से अग्नि लोक, फिर वायु लोक, फिर वरुण लोक, फिर आदित्य लोक, फिर इन्द्र लोक, फिर प्रजापति लोक, और फिर ब्रह्म लोक को प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: The progressive journey through the lokas (worlds) along the devayana path. Each loka represents a stage of purification and expansion of consciousness, culminating in Brahmaloka — the world of Brahma.
verses.wordMeaning: The progressive journey through the lokas (worlds) along the devayana path. Each loka represents a stage of purification and expansion of consciousness, culminating in Brahmaloka — the world of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: रितुरस्म्यर्तवोऽस्म्याकाशयोनेः सम्भूतो भार्यायै रेतः संवत्सरस्य तेजो भूतस्य भूतस्यात्मा भूतस्य त्वमात्मसि यस्त्वमसि सोऽहमस्मि ||
verses.transliteration: riturasmyartavo'smyākāśayoneḥ saṃbhūto bhāryāyai retaḥ saṃvatsarasya tejo bhūtasya bhūtasyātmā bhūtasya tvamātmasi yastvamasi so'hamasmi ||
verses.translation: I am the season. I am of the season. I am born in the space of the womb through the seed, as the light of the year, and as the embodied self of all beings. You are the self of the beings. That which you are, I am also that.
verses.hindi: मैं ऋतु हूँ, मैं ऋतु का हूँ। मैं गर्भ के आकाश में बीज से पैदा हूँ, वर्ष के प्रकाश के रूप में, और सभी प्राणियों के आत्मा के रूप में। तुम प्राणियों के आत्मा हो। जो तुम हो, मैं वही हूँ।
verses.commentary: The dialogue with the moon-god (Chandra) who represents time and seasons. The soul must recognize its identity with the cosmic principle of time and cycles.
verses.wordMeaning: The dialogue with the moon-god (Chandra) who represents time and seasons. The soul must recognize its identity with the cosmic principle of time and cycles.

verses.sanskrit: यजुदरः समसिर आसवृन्मूर्तिरव्यय स ब्रह्मेति विज्ञेय ऋषिर्ब्रह्ममयो महान् ||
verses.transliteration: yajudarāḥ samasira āsavṛnmūrtiravyaya sa brahmeti vijñeya ṛṣirbrahmamayo mahān ||
verses.translation: The seer, whose belly is Yaju, head is Saman, and form is Rik, he is to be known as the imperishable great Brahma.
verses.hindi: वह ऋषि, जिसका पेट यजुर्वेद है, सिर सामवेद है, और रूप ऋग्वेद है, उसे अविनाशी महान ब्रह्म के रूप में जानना चाहिए।
verses.commentary: The cosmic person whose body is the Vedas themselves. This is a vision of the universe as the body of Brahman, with each Veda representing a different aspect.
verses.wordMeaning: The cosmic person whose body is the Vedas themselves. This is a vision of the universe as the body of Brahman, with each Veda representing a different aspect.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणो ब्रह्मेति ह स्माह कौषीतकिः | तस्य ह वै एतस्य प्राणस्य ब्रह्मनो मनो दूतं चक्षुर्गोप्तृ श्रोत्रं संस्रवायितृ वाक्परिवेष्ट्री ||
verses.transliteration: prāṇo brahmeti ha smāha kauṣītakiḥ | tasya vai etasya prāṇasya brahmano mano dūtaṃ cakṣurgoptṛ śrotraṃ saṃsrāvayitṛ vākpariveṣṭrī ||
verses.translation: Prana is Brahman — so said Kaushitaki. Of this breath which is verily Brahma, the mind is the messenger, the eye is the protector, the ear the announcer, and speech the housekeeper.
verses.hindi: कौषीतकि ने कहा: प्राण ब्रह्म है। इस प्राण के लिए, जो वास्तव में ब्रह्म है, मन दूत है, आँख रक्षक है, कान घोषक है, और वाणी गृहस्थ है।
verses.commentary: The organs are servants of prana. Mind, eye, ear, speech — all function because prana animates them. When prana withdraws, all organs cease to function.
verses.wordMeaning: The organs are servants of prana. Mind, eye, ear, speech — all function because prana animates them. When prana withdraws, all organs cease to function.

verses.sanskrit: स प्राणो ब्रह्मेति ह स्माह पैङ्ग्यस्तस्य वै एतस्य प्राणस्य ब्रह्मनो वाच्परस्ताच्क्षुरारुन्धते चक्षुः परस्ताच्छोत्रमारुन्धते ||
verses.transliteration: sa prāṇo brahmeti ha smāha paiṅgyastasya vai etasya prāṇasya brahmano vācparastācakṣurārundhate cakṣuḥ parastācśotramārundhate ||
verses.translation: Prana is Brahman — so said Paingya. In this breath, on the upper side of speech the eye is enclosed, on the sides of the eye the ear is enclosed, on the inside of the ear the mind is enclosed.
verses.hindi: पैङ्ग्य ने कहा: प्राण ब्रह्म है। इस प्राण में, वाणी के ऊपरी भाग में आँख बंद है, आँख के किनारों पर कान बंद है, कान के अंदर मन बंद है।
verses.commentary: Paingya's vision of the nested structure of consciousness and organs. Each organ contains and is contained by others, all centered on prana.
verses.wordMeaning: Paingya's vision of the nested structure of consciousness and organs. Each organ contains and is contained by others, all centered on prana.

verses.sanskrit: अहं प्राणः प्रज्ञात्मा तं मामायुरमृतमित्युपास्स्व | आयुः प्राणः प्राणो ह्यायुः ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ prāṇaḥ prajñātmā taṃ māmāyuramṛtamityupāssva | āyuḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇo hyāyuḥ ||
verses.translation: I am prana — the conscious Self. Worship me as life, as immortality. Life is prana; prana is life.
verses.hindi: मैं प्राण हूँ — प्रज्ञात्मा (चेतन आत्मा)। मुझे आयु और अमृत के रूप में उपासना करो। आयु ही प्राण है और प्राण ही आयु है।
verses.commentary: Indra reveals his true identity: not the god of storms and thunder, but the prana — the conscious animating principle in all beings. "Prajnatma" — the Self that is pure consciousness — is the real Indra. The external mythology dissolves into inner truth: every god in the Vedic tradition points inward to an aspect of consciousness. To know Indra as prana is to find the divine not in the sky but in the very breath of life.
verses.wordMeaning: Indra reveals his true identity: not the god of storms and thunder, but the prana — the conscious animating principle in all beings. "Prajnatma" — the Self that is pure consciousness — is the real Indra. The external mythology dissolves into inner truth: every god in the Vedic tradition points inward to an aspect of consciousness. To know Indra as prana is to find the divine not in the sky but in the very breath of life.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणो वै सत्यं तस्मात् प्राणं वदन्ति सत्यं हि वै प्राणः | प्राणो हि वै सर्वं ज्योतिः प्राणो हि वै सर्वं वीर्यम् ||
verses.transliteration: prāṇo vai satyaṃ tasmāt prāṇaṃ vadanti satyaṃ hi vai prāṇaḥ | prāṇo hi vai sarvaṃ jyotiḥ prāṇo hi vai sarvaṃ vīryam ||
verses.translation: Prana is indeed truth; therefore they call prana truth, for prana is truly truth. Prana is indeed all light; prana is indeed all power.
verses.hindi: प्राण ही सत्य है; इसीलिए प्राण को सत्य कहते हैं, क्योंकि प्राण वास्तव में सत्य है। प्राण ही सब प्रकाश है; प्राण ही सब वीर्य है।
verses.commentary: The Kaushitaki Upanishad's central declaration on prana. Unlike other Upanishads that identify Brahman with consciousness or being, the Kaushitaki makes the radical claim that prana — the vital breath — is the fundamental reality. "Satyaṃ hi vai prāṇaḥ" — prana is truth itself, not merely a path to truth. "Sarvaṃ jyotiḥ" — all light, all illumination, derives from prana. "Sarvaṃ vīryam" — all power, all capacity for action, is prana. This is not physiology; it is ontology: prana is the ground of being, knowing, and acting.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kaushitaki Upanishad's central declaration on prana. Unlike other Upanishads that identify Brahman with consciousness or being, the Kaushitaki makes the radical claim that prana — the vital breath — is the fundamental reality. "Satyaṃ hi vai prāṇaḥ" — prana is truth itself, not merely a path to truth. "Sarvaṃ jyotiḥ" — all light, all illumination, derives from prana. "Sarvaṃ vīryam" — all power, all capacity for action, is prana. This is not physiology; it is ontology: prana is the ground of being, knowing, and acting.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 — Partial Definitions of Brahman
chapters.titleSanskrit: चतुर्थ अध्याय — ब्रह्म के आंशिक परिभाषा

verses.sanskrit: अथ ह वै गार्ग्यो बालाकिरानुचानः सम्स्पष्ट आस | सोऽवसद् उषीणरेषु सवसन् मत्स्येषु कुरुपाञ्चलेषु काशिविदेहेष्व् इति स हाजतसत्रुं काश्यमेऽब्रज्योवच ब्रह्म ते ब्रवाणीति ||
verses.transliteration: atha vai gārgyo bālākirānucānaḥ sampaṣṭa āsa | so'vasad uṣīṇareṣu savasan matsyeṣu kurupāñcaleṣu kāśivideheṣv iti sa hājatasastrau kāśyame'brajyovaca brahma te bravāṇīti ||
verses.translation: Now, Gargya Balaki was renowned as a famous person, for it was said of him that he lived among the people of Usinara, Matsya, Kurupancala and Kasivideha. He once went to Ajatasatru and said, "Let me speak about Brahman to you."
verses.hindi: अब गार्ग्य बालाकि प्रसिद्ध व्यक्ति थे, क्योंकि उनके बारे में कहा जाता था कि वे उषीणर, मत्स्य, कुरुपांचल और काशिविदेह के लोगों में रहते थे। वे एक बार अजातशत्रु के पास गए और कहा, "मैं तुम्हें ब्रह्म के बारे में बताऊं।"
verses.commentary: Gargya Balaki approaches King Ajatasatru with spiritual knowledge, representing the intellectual approach to Brahman through deities and external forms.
verses.wordMeaning: Gargya Balaki approaches King Ajatasatru with spiritual knowledge, representing the intellectual approach to Brahman through deities and external forms.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्ये बृहच्चन्द्रमसयन्नम् विद्युति सत्यं स्तनयित्नौ शब्दो वायविन्द्रो वैकुण्ठ आकाशे पूर्णम् अग्नौ विशाहिरित् अप्सु तेज इत्याधिदैवतम् ||
verses.transliteration: āditye bṛhaccandramasayannam vidyuti satyaṃ stanayitnau śabdo vāyavindro vaikuṇṭha ākāśe pūrṇam agnau viśāhirit apsu teja ityādhidaivatam ||
verses.translation: In the sun which is great, in the moon, in food, in lightning, in truth, in the sound of thunder, in wind, in Indra Vaikuntha, in space which is full, in fire, in water, in light — this is with reference to the deities.
verses.hindi: सूर्य में जो बड़ा है, चंद्रमा में, अन्न में, बिजली में, सत्य में, गर्जन के शब्द में, वायु में, इंद्र वैकुंठ में, आकाश में जो पूर्ण है, अग्नि में, जल में, प्रकाश में — यह देवताओं के संदर्भ में है।
verses.commentary: Gargya lists various deities and cosmic elements as Brahman. Each is a partial truth — a window into the absolute but not the absolute itself.
verses.wordMeaning: Gargya lists various deities and cosmic elements as Brahman. Each is a partial truth — a window into the absolute but not the absolute itself.

verses.sanskrit: स होवाच बालाकिः य एवैष आदित्ये पुरुषस्तमेवाहमुपास इति तं होवाच अजातशत्रुः मा मैतस्मिन्समवादयिष्ठो बृहत्पण्डरवासोऽतिष्ठः सर्वेषां भूतानां मूर्धेति व अहमेतमुपास इति ||
verses.transliteration: sa hovāca bālakiḥ ya evaiṣa āditye puruṣastam evāham upāsa iti taṃ hovāca ajātaśatruḥ mā maitasminsamavādayiṣṭho bṛhatpaṇḍaravāso'tiṣṭhaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdheti va ahametam upāsa iti ||
verses.translation: Then Balaki said, "That person in the sun, him I worship." Ajatasatru said, "Please do not make me debate on him. I meditate upon him who is the great, who wears white garments, the highest and the head of all beings."
verses.hindi: तब बालाकि ने कहा, "सूर्य में जो पुरुष है, उसकी मैं उपासना करता हूँ।" अजातशत्रु ने कहा, "कृपया मुझे उस पर बहस न करने दो। मैं उसकी उपासना करता हूँ जो महान है, जो सफेद वस्त्र पहनता है, सर्वोच्च है और सभी प्राणियों का शिर है।"
verses.commentary: Ajatasatru rejects Balaki's external worship and points to the inner reality — the Self as the head of all beings, not the external sun.
verses.wordMeaning: Ajatasatru rejects Balaki's external worship and points to the inner reality — the Self as the head of all beings, not the external sun.

verses.sanskrit: तत ऊ ह बालाकिः तुष्निमास तं होवाच अजातशत्रुः एतावन्नू बालक इति एतावदिति होवाच बालाकिः तं होवाच अजातशत्रुः मृषा वै किल मा संवादिष्ठ ब्रह्म ते ब्रवाणीति ||
verses.transliteration: tata ū hā bālakiḥ tuṣnimāsa taṃ hovāca ajātaśatruḥ etāvannū bālaka iti etāvaditi hovāca bālakiḥ taṃ hovāca ajātaśatruḥ mṛṣā vai kila mā saṃvādiṣṭha brahma te bravāṇīti ||
verses.translation: Thereafter, Balaki became silent. To him Ajatasatru said, "Balaki, is that all?" "That is all," replied Balaki. To him Ajatasatru said, "Vainly did you engage me in this discussion, saying, 'Let me tell you about Brahman.'
verses.hindi: उसके बाद, बालाकि चुप हो गए। अजातशत्रु ने उनसे कहा, "बालाकि, क्या बस इतना ही?" "बस इतना ही," बालाकि ने उत्तर दिया। अजातशत्रु ने कहा, "व्यर्थ में तुमने मुझे इस चर्चा में लगाया, कहकर 'मैं तुम्हें ब्रह्म बताऊंगा।'
verses.commentary: Balaki's knowledge is exhausted — he has only external, partial definitions. Ajatasatru points out that this is not true knowledge of Brahman.
verses.wordMeaning: Balaki's knowledge is exhausted — he has only external, partial definitions. Ajatasatru points out that this is not true knowledge of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: होवाच यो वै बालक एतेषां पुरुषाणां कर्ता यस्य वै तत्कर्म स वेदितव्य इति तत ऊ ह बालाकिः समित्पनिः प्रतिचक्रम उपायनीति ||
verses.transliteration: hovāca yo vai bālaka eteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ kartā yasya vai tat karma sa veditavya iti tata ū hā bālakiḥ samitpaniḥ praticakrama upāyanīti ||
verses.translation: He said, "Who is the doer among the persons, whose work all this is, he alone should be known." Thereupon, Balaki approached with fuel in his hand, saying, "I approach you as student."
verses.hindi: उन्होंने कहा, "इन सभी पुरुषों में कर्ता कौन है, जिसका यह सब काम है, उसी को जानना चाहिए।" तब बालाकि समित (ईध) लेकर पास आए और कहा, "मैं शिष्य के रूप में आता हूँ।"
verses.commentary: The pointer to the true doer — not the external deities but the inner Self that animates all.
verses.wordMeaning: The pointer to the true doer — not the external deities but the inner Self that animates all.
